validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: High, and higher than the last plan's 78, because the disputed finding is no longer a reading. I booted the production build, signed up through the real form, and measured the layout in a real browser at four viewports and at the schema's maximum name length: no overflow anywhere. The attribution is what makes me confident rather than merely hopeful — stripping min-w-0 from the nav reproduces QA's 548px and 318.84px to the decimal, and the padding-forced 532px too, so the finding is explained rather than dismissed. The three review findings are each confirmed by reading the exact line, and the suite is green at 86 tests. What holds me below the high 90s is one thing I cannot close from here: I cannot inspect the build QA actually ran, so I can prove main is correct and prove what QA saw, but not that no reachable build still lacks the class. That is why AC-1 is written as a regression guard QA repeats rather than a criterion anyone takes on trust, and why AC-5 exists to stop a later implementer editing a layout that measures correct.

validated_work_order.root_cause: Two independent causes and one non-cause. (1) The BUG-4 guard encodes a ceiling syntax rather than the concept: /max-w-\[\d/ means 'a bracketed max-width whose value starts with an ASCII digit', but the intent is 'no max-width ceiling on the display name'. Every bracket-valued Tailwind max-width carries a bracket, so the digit is an unnecessary narrowing three ordinary spellings slip past. (2) The fixture passes an element as Shell's children that duplicates one Shell already renders, so it asserts a DOM shape the application cannot produce — and React logs no validateDOMNesting warning for main-in-main, so it fails silently. (3) The three files were written without a final newline and nothing in the toolchain enforces one. NOT a cause: the QA 360px overflow. min-w-0 on the nav is present on main and load-bearing — removing it alone reproduces QA's 548px and 318.84px exactly. The build QA measured predates that class.

cases: the display-name link carries no bracketed max-width, so a ceiling written max-w-[9rem], max-w-[120px] or max-w-[--cap] is caught as well as a digit-valued one
the Shell fixture composition contains exactly one <main>, with no <main> nested inside another
the display-name link does not carry shrink-0, so it remains the flex item that gives ground while Groups and the sign-out form stay pinned
the nav still carries min-w-0, the class whose removal reproduces the 548px overflow and whose loss every other assertion in the case would miss

validated_work_order.understanding: Five findings: four from the review of PR #13 (now main at 6c423f4) and one from QA. I re-measured rather than re-read, because the last plan was rejected for asserting the QA overflow was already handled on the strength of finding the right class names in the markup — and a browser was available to me. It was. Chromium runs headless on this runner (the dbus/GCM stderr is not a failure; --dump-dom exits 0), so I installed dependencies, ran npm run sdlc:serve, signed up through the real /sign-up form over CDP, and measured the top bar at 360x640. Result: documentElement.scrollWidth is 360 against a clientWidth of 360 on / and on /settings. The name link measures 108.77px wide, not 318.84px — it shrank, and the Sign out control's right edge lands at 344, inside the viewport. The finding does not reproduce on main. I then attributed QA's number rather than assuming it stale: stripping min-w-0 from the nav in the live page moves scrollWidth to exactly 548 and the name link to exactly 318.84px, QA's figure to the decimal; stripping min-w-0 together with both shrink-0 classes reproduces 548 again, and additionally forcing padding-inline to 0 gives 532, the second figure in QA's report. QA drove a build in which min-w-0 was absent from the nav, and the chain that fixes it is present and working on main. I checked it is not merely present but effective: no overflow at 320, 360, 414 or 1280, and at the schema's maximum 80-character name (an unbroken W x 80), where scrollWidth still equals clientWidth and the name link clamps to 108.77px at 360. At 1280 the 80-character name renders in full at 1012.77px, so the ceiling this chain replaced is not reintroduced and BUG-4 stays fixed. That also answers the reviewer's second objection: min-w-[44px] on the name link is a floor of 44px, and the link shrinks to 108.77 — above its floor, so the floor is not what pinned it, and the span's truncate is what renders the ellipsis once the link narrows. The finding is dispositioned as not reproducing, with the measurement recorded, and needs no code change. The three review findings are real and I confirmed each by reading the file. (1) The BUG-4 guard at tests/components/ui.test.tsx:307 is /max-w-\[\d/, matching only a bracket followed by an ASCII digit, so max-w-[9rem], max-w-[--cap] and an inline style={{maxWidth:'120px'}} all pass. (2) The fixture at :294 renders <main /> inside a Shell that already renders <main id="main"> (src/components/shell.tsx:18); the product never renders that shape, since src/ emits <main> only in shell.tsx:18 and the two signed-out auth pages. (3) All three files this ticket touches lack a trailing newline: tail -c 1 | xxd -p returns 7d for top-bar.tsx, 7d for shell.tsx, 3b for ui.test.tsx. One correction to the review's premises, re-confirmed: finding 3 says the repo is otherwise consistent about trailing newlines. It is not — 44 tracked .ts/.tsx/.mjs/.json/.css files lack one, including package.json and eslint.config.mjs. Fixing the three this ticket touches is still right; the rest is a separate decision. On the reviewer's objection that QA cannot sign in: .sdlc/config.yml sets qa_auth.mode: none, but sign-up is an unauthenticated flow and the app's own sign-up creates a session and redirects to / — I did exactly this over CDP and reached / signed in. The path is /sign-up, not /signup: the config's qa_auth.signup_url says "/signup" but src/app/sign-up/page.tsx is the only sign-up route, so the config value points at a 404. I cannot change that (reserved path), so this plan routes QA to /sign-up explicitly.
